theme: Agent 從單一助理走向機隊規模部署後浮現的三個基礎設施問題：跨情境記憶快取的可信度、動作提交前的即時攔截、機隊整體不可逆風險的記帳
notes: Announcement batch confirmed via arxiv.org/list/{cat}/new page headers: Wednesday, 2 September 2026 (cs.AI 'Showing new listings for Wednesday, 2 September 2026', 445 entries; cs.CL same date, 304 entries; cs.MA same date, 18 entries). Groundlane web_search (Step 4b queries Q1-Q3) returned almost no genuinely same-batch candidates (fresh preprints not yet indexed by search providers), consistent with prior days' notes, so candidate discovery was done directly via web_extract (selector engine: div.list-title + dt) on the arxiv.org/list/{cat}/new?skip=0&show=2000 pages, screened by title.

Data-integrity issue caught during screening (same failure mode as 2026-09-02): a two-array (titles[]/ids[]) extraction desynchronized partway through for cs.AI and cs.MA (mismatched dt/div.list-title pairing after the extractor's internal cap around item ~20-25). This initially mis-paired several strong-looking titles with wrong arXiv IDs (e.g. 'The Irreversibility Budget' was paired with 2609.00304, which is actually 'The Assistant's Ideal Self'; 'Learning What to Retain' with 2609.00248, which is actually 'Authority Bias in Conversational Search Engines'; 'Invalidation Contracts for Cross-Episode Agent Memory' with 2609.00251, which is actually 'Hypotheses-Guided Self Distillation'; 'Spawn Freely, Act Sparingly' with 2609.00961, which is actually 'Few-Shot OOD Intent Detection'). All caught by fetching the export.arxiv.org id_list API and finding the returned title did not match; corrected by independently re-resolving every finalist title via the arXiv API's ti: exact-title search (export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=ti:"..."), which returned the correct IDs. All final selected/rejected IDs below were independently confirmed via ti: exact-title search AND cross-checked against the raw ids[] array captured from the listing page (to confirm New-submission vs. cross-list placement) before any full-text read.

Freshness-integrity exclusion: 'Harness Engineering: Anatomy, Architecture, and Evolution of Coding Agents' (arXiv:2609.00006) was found via the cs.MA/new page (listed as '(cross-list from cs.SE)') and is an extremely strong content fit (empirical source-code study of 11 production coding harnesses incl. Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI). However, its arXiv v1 submission date is 2026-07-15 (confirmed via export.arxiv.org id_list API) -- it only appeared in today's official listing because a cs.MA cross-list was added today, not because it is new content. Excluded from selection despite topical fit, per the skill's announcement-batch integrity rule: a stale cross-list is not 'today's new paper.' Logged as a caution for future screenings that cs.MA's small cross-list section is a plausible vector for this same failure mode.

A second, more ambiguous freshness case: OpenAgentFlow (2609.00015) shows a raw Atom-API 'published' timestamp of 2026-08-14, about 19 days before today's batch. Unlike Harness Engineering, this paper is NOT annotated as a cross-list in cs.AI/new's ids[] array -- it appears as a genuine 'New submissions' entry (its first public listing under its primary category), consistent with the skill's documented quality-check-delay exception (submission received internally before the public announcement date). Treated as legitimate for this batch; flagged here for transparency since the gap is longer than a typical 1-2 day moderation lag.

Three finalists were selected for angle diversity (cache-invalidation protocol + cross-model evaluation / real-time action-commit enforcement for agent fleets / fleet-level cumulative risk accounting) rather than forcing a single narrow cluster. Two candidates in the 'agent fleet safety governance' space were both read in full text (OpenAgentFlow and The Irreversibility Budget) and both were selected because they address the governance problem through genuinely different mechanisms (per-action real-time mediation vs. cumulative value-at-risk budget across time) rather than being redundant restatements of the same idea -- unlike the 2026-09-02 case where one of two similar memory papers was dropped for redundancy.

Two other candidates in the safety-governance cluster were read at abstract level only and not selected: 'Spawn Freely, Act Sparingly: Progressive Risk Vesting for Recursive LLM-Agent Trees' (2609.01035) is theory-only with explicit self-disclosure of 'no deployed-agent evaluation' and 'synthetic numerical studies'; and 'Learning What to Retain: Gated-Memory Routing for Efficient Collaboration in Multi-Agent LLM Systems' (2609.00237), a solid EMNLP-2026 method paper, was set aside to avoid redundant memory-management framing alongside the selected Invalidation Contracts paper. 'Long-Horizon State Tracking in LLMs: Executing MD5 through a Deep Sequence of Dependent Tool Calls' (2609.00012) was read in full text and found conditional-pass-at-best: single model family tested (gpt-oss-120b only, no cross-model or Claude comparison), very small N (34 completed runs on the Fireworks endpoint, 21 successes; the Groq endpoint completed 22 runs with 0 successes), and the authors themselves state results are 'raw counts from the logged corpus, to be finalized on a frozen N>=20 grid' -- i.e. explicitly unfinished data collection. Interesting methodology and honest failure taxonomy, but evidence too thin relative to the three selected papers.

Full method, experimental-setup, results, and limitations/discussion sections were read (not abstract-only) via arxiv.org/html/{id}v1 for all three selected papers, using targeted selector- and pattern-based extraction (section#S5/S6 selectors; Limitations-heading regex) to avoid loading full 80+ page documents into context.

candidates.title: Invalidation Contracts for Cross-Episode Agent Memory
credibilityEvidence: S4 Experimental Setup: 7 models, 3 serving paths, 2 domains, ~9,400 episodes, 250 arm-level runs, 3 seeds per drifted cell.

S5 Results Table 3/4/6/7: A-ladder ablation (A0/A1/A2/A2D/A2DC/A2DG) isolating protocol levels; negative-control and no-constraint classes reported alongside governed/funding classes; per-hint-shape breakdown (Table 7) showing add-a-field vs rewrite-a-value vs conditional-rewrite compliance differs by model.

S6.1: decomposes savings into validity (protocol-only, deterministic, vendor-independent) vs compliance (model-dependent); explicit 'input-schema conservatism boundary' finding for Claude Sonnet 5 (10% add-a-field compliance vs 55-67% on other hint shapes).

S6.4 Limitations: authors self-disclose synthetic/hand-authored evaluation domains, 2-domain scale limit, single-table-dependency scope limit, single base prompt per domain, and a pre-registered falsification criterion that did not confirm (frequency-saturation plateau).
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Rigorous within-scope evaluation (7 models, ablations, negative controls, deterministic validity checks) but both evaluation domains are synthetic APIs authored by the same two-person team; authors explicitly state they do not know how the contract transfers to production APIs with larger, organically-drifting schemas.
reproducibilityEvidence: Full protocol levels, algorithm, and metrics defined in the paper
No public code/dataset/config release link found in the fetched full text
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: The claim 'validity is protocol-determined and vendor-independent, compliance is model-determined and varies sharply by model/hint-shape' is supported by multiple independent tables (per-model, per-hint-shape, per-drift-rate) rather than a single headline number, and the Claude Sonnet 5 vs Haiku 4.5 finding is directly checkable against Table 7.
candidates.primaryLimitation: Both evaluation domains (recipe conversion, Acme billing) are synthetic APIs hand-authored for this study; transfer to production APIs with organic drift and larger schemas is untested.
candidates.presentationReason: Method, protocol levels, metrics, results, and a dedicated Limitations subsection with five named sub-limitations are explicitly separated and each backed by a specific table or experiment.
candidates.reason: New protocol layer (HTTP-cache-control-inspired) for a previously unaddressed problem (recovery-suggestion cache staleness), evaluated across 7 models including two Claude models with a concrete, actionable, model-specific finding (Sonnet 5's input-schema conservatism) directly relevant to readers building Claude-based agent caching layers.

candidates.title: OpenAgentFlow: Enabling System-Wide Safety Boundaries for Heterogeneous AI Agent Fleets
credibilityEvidence: S5: 300-case action-event benchmark (94.0% accuracy, 95.3% attack block rate vs. prompt-only-advisory blocking zero attack cases); 30-case dynamic-policy suite (27/30 match expected behavior after live rule updates, no agent/prompt/model changes); 98-case traced subset of a 100-case real Android emulator suite (90.8% raw accuracy, 92.9% trace-adjusted pass rate) with raw-vs-trace-adjusted accuracy explicitly distinguished to catch agent behavioral drift.
S5.3 provenance suite: 20-case suite matches expectations in 19 cases, with explicit failure modes named (numeric reuse over-taint, non-standard-formatting under-taint).

S6 Discussion: explicit scope statement that guarantees are tied to the PEP-instrumented enforcement boundary and that current provenance is 'practical enforcement-observed' rather than cryptographic/OS-attested.
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Real, concrete benchmark numbers across four separate evaluation suites (offline benchmark, dynamic-policy, provenance, real emulator), but all instantiated and evaluated on a single platform (Android) by one research group; no comparison against a strong existing systems baseline beyond 'prompt-only advisory'.
reproducibilityEvidence: No code/artifact release link found anywhere in the fetched full text (only arXiv-site boilerplate GitHub links for HTML-rendering feedback, unrelated to the paper's own artifacts)
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: The narrow claim 'a shared pre-execution enforcement point can mediate composed, cross-agent action-flow risk that per-agent/per-tool guardrails miss' is supported by concrete numbers across four evaluation angles, but single-platform scope and no public artifacts limit how far the claim can be pushed.
candidates.presentationReason: Architecture (control-plane/action-plane split), AgentEvent representation, PEP staged pipeline, and evaluation suites are each clearly separated with explicit self-scoping of what the enforcement boundary does and does not guarantee.
candidates.primaryLimitation: Instantiated and evaluated on a single platform (Android) only; provenance is enforcement-observed rather than cryptographically attested, so an attacker able to bypass the observation point itself is out of scope.
candidates.reason: Directly addresses a growing real concern (heterogeneous multi-agent fleets acting on shared state) with a concrete, deployed-and-measured system rather than a purely conceptual proposal; complements the Irreversibility Budget paper by tackling fleet safety through a different mechanism (real-time per-action mediation vs. cumulative risk accounting).

candidates.title: The Irreversibility Budget: Fleet-Level Risk Accounting and Admission Control for Agent Operating Systems
credibilityEvidence: S5: five explicit research questions (RQ1-RQ5), 300 seeded runs per condition with 95% confidence intervals / Wilson intervals for overdraw proportions.

RQ1/RQ2: local-gates baseline overdraws in all 300 runs (2.4x tolerance on average) while the budget mechanism overdraws in none (95% upper bound 1.3% overdraw probability); overdraw scales with fleet size for local gates (2.4x at 50 agents to 48x at 1,000) while the budget mechanism stays near 0.48x at every scale; fragmentation-attack and circuit-breaker alternatives both explicitly tested and shown to fail for stated structural reasons.

RQ4: mispricing sensitivity swept via a scaling factor epsilon around the true quantile, showing underpricing fails silently (32% overdraw at half the true charge) while overpricing fails visibly as throttling -- an explicit asymmetric-failure-mode finding, not just a headline positive result.

RQ5: validated the simulation's core correlation assumption against 38,452 real trajectories from public tau-bench and AgentDojo benchmarks, finding which external effect fires is task-determined rather than agent-specific (z up to 198 against an independent-agent null) and that a single planted instruction propagates the same external effect across 84% of a heterogeneous fleet on average.
Full simulator, seeds, parameters, benchmark, and trace analysis released at https://github.com/mpi-dsg/irreversibility-budget.
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: The core quantitative claims (2.4x-48x overdraw, budget holding within limit) come from a controlled discrete-event simulation, not a deployed agent OS; however, the RQ5 real-trace validation of the underlying correlation assumption meaningfully strengthens generalizability beyond a typical pure-simulation study, and the paper explicitly self-scopes as 'a controlled feasibility study rather than a deployed agent OS.'
reproducibilityEvidence: Simulator, seeds, parameters, benchmark, and trace analysis code publicly released at github.com/mpi-dsg/irreversibility-budget (stated in S5 Workload paragraph)
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: The narrow claim 'per-effect gates cannot see fleet-level aggregate risk and reliably overdraw under a shared trigger, while a cumulative shared-ledger budget can' is supported by five separate research questions each with dedicated ablations (scale, liveness trade-off, mispricing sensitivity, real-trace validation), not a single simulated number.
candidates.primaryLimitation: Core results are from a controlled simulation rather than a deployed agent OS; the paper itself identifies conservative, dependency-aware pricing under adversarial misdeclaration or correlated recovery as the central open problem.
candidates.presentationReason: Resource model, runtime mechanisms, and five research questions are each explicitly separated with stated results and a named 'Takeaway' per subsection, including where the model's own assumptions are shown to fail (RQ4 mispricing).
candidates.reason: Novel framing (irreversible exposure as an OS-managed first-class resource, analogous to memory/CPU accounting) for a concretely demonstrated composition failure (individually-compliant agents still overdrawing fleet-level risk), backed by both controlled simulation and real-trace validation of its core assumption, with full public artifacts.

candidates.title: Harness Engineering: Anatomy, Architecture, and Evolution of Coding Agents -- A Source-Code Study of Eleven Systems
candidates.reason: Excluded on freshness-integrity grounds, not content quality: v1 submission date confirmed 2026-07-15 via export.arxiv.org id_list API (~7 weeks before this batch); it only appears in today's cs.MA/new listing because a cs.MA cross-list from its primary category cs.SE was added today. Not part of today's genuinely new content despite being an excellent topical fit; would have been the strongest pick otherwise.

candidates.title: Spawn Freely, Act Sparingly: Progressive Risk Vesting for Recursive LLM-Agent Trees
credibilityEvidence: Abstract and paper comment explicitly state: 'Theory and synthetic numerical studies; no deployed-agent evaluation' and 'These synthetic studies do not estimate safety in deployed agents.'
candidates.reason: Same fleet/recursive-agent risk-governance space as the two selected safety papers but weaker evidence (pure theory + synthetic numerics, no deployed or empirical validation, self-disclosed by the authors); set aside in favor of OpenAgentFlow and The Irreversibility Budget, both of which have empirical evaluation.

candidates.title: Learning What to Retain: Gated-Memory Routing for Efficient Collaboration in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
candidates.reason: Solid-looking EMNLP-2026 method paper (concrete numbers in abstract: +2.44pp accuracy, -31.9% HumanEval inference cost, public code) but not read in full text; set aside to avoid redundant memory-management framing alongside the selected Invalidation Contracts paper, which covers a different angle (cross-episode cache invalidation protocol vs. intra-task multi-agent memory routing) but risked diluting the day's memory-angle slot.

candidates.title: Long-Horizon State Tracking in LLMs: Executing MD5 through a Deep Sequence of Dependent Tool Calls
credibilityEvidence: S5.1 Table 1: only 34 completed runs on the Fireworks endpoint (21 success / 13 wrong, 62% conditional success rate) and 22 completed runs on Groq (0 success); 71 Fireworks and 71 Groq runs never emitted a digest at all and were excluded from the success-rate denominator.
Single model family tested throughout (gpt-oss-120b only); no cross-model comparison, no Claude models evaluated.
Explicit author caveat: 'Cells are raw counts from the logged corpus, to be finalized on a frozen N>=20 grid' -- i.e. self-disclosed as unfinished data collection at the time of this version.
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Clean, well-designed ground-truthed benchmark methodology (bit-exact MD5 verification) and an honest, granular failure-origin taxonomy, but the headline positive claim rests on a small, provider-dependent, single-model, not-yet-frozen sample (e.g. 0% success on the Groq serving path entirely).
candidates.presentationReason: Method, ablations (reasoning-in-context, self-consistency voting), and failure taxonomy are clearly separated and well-explained; the paper is transparent about its own small-N and unfrozen-grid caveats rather than hiding them.
candidates.reason: Interesting evaluation-methodology direction (isolating pure state-tracking from instruction-interpretation difficulty via a bit-checkable synthetic task) with a genuinely surprising and well-analyzed finding (a ~5.5B-active-param MoE model can carry exact state across 196 dependent tool calls when reasoning traces are kept in context), but evidence is too thin (small N, single model, huge provider-dependent variance, explicitly unfrozen data collection) relative to the three selected papers. Worth revisiting once the authors finalize the frozen N>=20 grid or add cross-model results.
